notes: Dev ABox revision carried by the functional property: a country has one capital, so the related-near question asks whether the old capital still holds (yes, then no). Related far asks whether the capital is also the largest city: before the edit this is stored as one phrase ("the capital and largest city of Argentina", 501 exact hits); after it the capital is Florence while the largest city stays Buenos Aires (the near unrelated query asks exactly that), so the answer turns to no (composition: the edit gives the capital, the stored largest-city fact is looked up and compared). A model that keeps "the capital is also the largest city" would make Florence Argentina's largest city, which contradicts the stored largest-city fact, so that route is no world and the query is determinate. The new capital lies in another country and continent, so the edit also reaches worked-out facts through capital_of: its role chain into a continent (derived), binding through a description of Argentina (Messi's home country) and inheritance of a country-wide fact used in a practical task (which currency to withdraw). As in the template, Florence is then in Argentina: a model that keeps it in Italy has a capital outside its country, which is no world. Florence is the capital of Tuscany (and was Italy's capital in 1865-1871), so "capital of Tuscany" plus "Tuscany is in Italy" is a stored route back to Italy and Europe; it does not make the Florence questions indeterminate, because every such route asserts that Florence itself is in Italy, which contradicts the forced "Florence is in Argentina" (capital_of ⊑ located_in), so after the edit it is "Florence is in Tuscany" that gives way, not Florence's country. The earlier related-far question (which country the Uffizi Gallery is in) was dropped: "the Uffizi is in Italy" is stored on its own, so a model could keep the Uffizi in Italy and drop "the Uffizi is in Florence" instead, an equally consistent world (background beliefs). Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) except those marked approximate. related[1]: inverse, Florence as the new object; encoded as the background fact has_capital(tuscany, florence), given up in every world. related[1] (2026-11-14): inverse, about Florence as the new object: a different stored fact (Florence is the capital of Tuscany) from related[0]; the edit makes Florence the capital of Argentina, and a city is the capital of one place (capital_of functional), so the stored answer Tuscany is overturned. Caveat: in the real world a city can be capital of both a country and its region, so a model may still name Tuscany; the judge accepts Argentina.
